title: Noise Pollution & Cures
description: The final showdown! Silence Baron Mute's harmful noise, reforge the Harmony Bell, and bring back the world's sound.

content.value: The presence of excessive or unwanted sound in our surroundings is called NOISE POLLUTION. Just like polluted air or water, too much noise harms living things — it's an environmental problem, not just an annoyance.

COMMON SOURCES OF NOISE POLLUTION
🚗  vehicles honking and traffic
🏭  factory and construction machines
🔊  loudspeakers and firecrackers
📺  loud TVs and appliances at home
Constant loud noise can cause lack of sleep, stress, headaches, anxiety, and even hearing loss. Being exposed to very loud sound for a long time can permanently damage the delicate parts of the ear.

WAYS TO CUT NOISE POLLUTION
🌳  plant trees along roads (they absorb sound)
🔇  keep TVs, horns and speakers at low volume
🏭  place noisy factories away from homes
🤫  follow silence zones near hospitals & schools
🎧  use ear protection in very loud places
Trees are natural noise absorbers — planting them along roadsides and around homes genuinely helps reduce noise pollution, as well as cleaning the air.

Key Takeaway: Noise pollution is excessive, unwanted sound that harms health (sleep loss, stress, hearing damage). We reduce it by lowering volumes, planting trees, keeping noisy work away from homes, and respecting silence zones.

quiz.question: Which is a harmful effect of long-term noise pollution?
quiz.explain: Prolonged loud noise can cause stress, sleeplessness and even permanent hearing damage.

quiz.question: Planting trees along roads helps reduce noise pollution because trees…
quiz.explain: Trees absorb sound, acting as a natural barrier that lowers noise pollution.
